newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease in caution, off lows on suppor.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease in caution, off lows on suppor.

text.p: Istanbul shares edged lower on Monday amid caution prompted by upcoming parliamentary votes on corruption probes against deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, but recovered from lows on support, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 .XU100 ended down one point, or 0.06 percent at 1,554, after rebounding from an early low of 1,516. Daily volume fell sharply to 18.87 trillion lira from Friday's 28.38 trillion.

"Both sellers and buyers were weak. Political uneasiness is negatively affecting the market. The upcoming votes raised political uncertainty and this sentiment may persist until the weekend," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.
Brokers said selling was awaited today because of the parliamentary debates set for Tuesday and Wednesday, but support was also expected at around the index's 1,500 mark.

Parliament will debate two corruption allegations against Ciller on Tuesday and another one on Wednesday. All probes were previously rejected by parliamentary commissions, but a vote in the general assembly will be final.
The market is also worried about two censure motions filed by leftist parties against the Islamist-led government, scheduled to be taken up in parliament on February 25.
Brokers said the market also lacked a motive after the recent strong rally which carried the index up 74.2 percent from end-1996 to an all-time high closing of 1,700 on January 27.

Of the 238 shares traded, 106 shares declined, 77 advanced and 55 finished stable. The IMKB Industrial .XUSIN firmed 0.43 percent to 1,619, the IMKB Services .XUHIZ fell 1.74 percent to 1,415 and the IMKB Financial .XUMAL edged up 0.06 percent to 1,574.

Actives were led by synthetic fibre and pet bottle maker Sasa, up 500 lira at 11,750, steel producer Izmir Demir Celik, up 75 lira at 2,250 and largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, down 250 lira at 20,750. They made up 17.4 percent of the total turnover.
